title: Clinical evidence of bone apposition and potential osseointegration in additively manufactured subperiosteal implants: a report of three cases
html: Subperiosteal implants were historically conceived as fixation-based devices rather than osseointegrated implants and were progressively abandoned due to unfavorable long-term outcomes. Recent advances in digital planning and additive manufacturing have led to the reintroduction of custom-made titanium subperiosteal implants; however, direct clinical evidence of osteointegration in humans has not been reported. This case series presents three patients rehabilitated with additively manufactured titanium subperiosteal implants who underwent surgical re-entry for the removal of loosened osteosynthesis screws associated with recurrent, non-infective inflammatory episodes.
